config.classes_note: Two classes, each sourced from the field by locus: Search Arena as a human-preference leaderboard, a ranking of AI models (B1's and B2's card titles, B3, B4, B8; the class is model rankings, not ranking as such, which the archive names everywhere as an operator, R_rank, of search), and the class of systems it rates, search-augmented language models and their citations (B3, B4). The second is the class of the entity's object, not the entity: an O-class candidate on it is admitted only where the archive applies its own category to search-augmented answer systems' citation, attribution or preference in a sentence that bears on what the leaderboard measures (its unit, the vote, the citation finding); a sentence on one named answer surface (Google's AI Overview, Perplexity, ChatGPT search) as itself is a claim on that surface and not admitted here. The aliases are the entity's name, its operator's domain and former names (LMArena, LM Arena, Chatbot Arena, LMSYS), the dataset paper's identifier and first author; 'LMSYS' and 'LM Arena' are case-sensitive. 'Arena' alone is not an alias (it is common English). Admission by reading (§3.4): a candidate is admitted when its sentence or paragraph makes a claim bearing on Search Arena or on Arena's leaderboards as the class the entity belongs to (what it is, its unit and method, its findings on citation, its standing as a ranking surface, a measure taken on it); a bare mention, a link list, a model ranking cited from Arena as evidence for something else, or a generic use of 'leaderboard' about another object is not a claim on the entity.
